paragraphs: Apple will reportedly put its own modems in every iPhone released next year, with no Qualcomm hardware left inside.
The move would conclude a years-long push to cut Qualcomm out of the iPhone. But Apple won’t be fully done with its old rival, thanks to a fresh patent deal.

Apple spent nearly a decade (and billions of dollars) trying to do something that once looked almost impossible: Kick Qualcomm out of the iPhone. The Apple C1 modem that debuted in last year’s iPhone 16e got the ball rolling in earnest, the C1X ramped things up later that year in the iPhone Air, and now the total replacement of Qualcomm’s hardware appears to be in sight.
Gurman reported that Apple has poured in tens of billions of dollars into its modem effort over the span of eight years.

The current lineup is split. The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo use Apple’s C2 modem worldwide, but a TechInsights teardown of the iPhone 18 Pro Max found Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X80 modem inside. Apple has not explained why the U.S. model is different.

Qualcomm announced on September 24 that it renewed its global patent license agreement with Apple. The new deal will go into effect April 1, 2027. The chipmaker did not disclose the length or financial terms of the deal.

Apple’s original license took effect April 1, 2019, after a sprawling legal battle between the two companies over royalties. That license ran six years, with an option to extend for two more. Apple used that option, with the agreement now pushing to the end of March 2027.
Importantly, the renewal covers patents, not chip supply. Apple can use its own models, but it will need to pay royalties on Qualcomm’s cellular technology.
